title: Threshold-driven mitigation plans for regional tier routing and model variant swaps
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Scope: Implement a threshold-driven mitigation layer for the router that automatically decides when to shift traffic across regions, between tiers (hosted vs dedicated), and to lower-latency model variants. This ticket covers the trigger detection windows, the decision logic for mitigation mode selection (probabilistic reroute, mode swap, or hard cutover), and the basic circuit-breaker state machine for route isolation. Goal: reduce customer-facing errors and tail latency during transient overloads while minimizing unnecessary model swaps that increase cost or reduce quality.
acceptance_criteria: Router publishes per-route rolling metrics (1m, 5m) for 429, timeout, 5xx, p95/p99 latency
Configurable trigger rules accepted by router policy engine and editable via Console (UI task separate)
Behavior: when configured thresholds are crossed, router enters a mitigation mode (soft-probabilistic reroute or full failover) per policy and logs decision events
Circuit-breaker transitions (CLOSED -> SOFT_OPEN -> OPEN -> PROBATION -> CLOSED) implemented with cooldown and exponential backoff
Automated tests that simulate 429 spikes, slow tail latencies, and 5xx bursts validate that mitigation reduces user-visible errors by >= 80% in staging
Monitoring: new dashboards show mitigation activations, percent traffic shifted, model-variant swaps, and success/failure rates; alerts for unexpected thrash
proposed_solution: Design a pluggable rule engine in the router that evaluates multiple signals using short and medium windows. Rules can combine signals (e.g., 1m 429 rate AND 5m p95 above threshold). When a rule fires, the engine picks a mitigation policy from ranked candidates: 1) probabilistic thinning to lower-cost tier, 2) swap to a quantized/low-latency model variant, 3) regional cutover to a healthy region. Introduce a stateful circuit-breaker per route with a SOFT_OPEN state where only a portion of traffic is redirected (to avoid immediate capacity shock). Reopen uses success-based probation and an exponential backoff on subsequent failures. Use token-based counters and a small distributed cache for cross-router signal aggregation to avoid noisy-local decisions.
detection_and_thresholds: 429 spike: rolling 1-minute 429 fraction > 0.5% AND 5-minute avg > 0.2% triggers SOFT_OPEN
Timeouts: request timeout (>= configured RPC timeout) p99 > 2% over 5 minutes triggers MODEL_SWAP to low-latency variant
Server errors: sustained 5xx rate > 0.1% for 3 consecutive minutes triggers OPEN for that route in the region
Latency regression: p95 > SLO_target * 1.6 for 3m triggers probabilistic thinning
Cost-quality safeguard: do not swap to lower-quality variant unless historical eval score drop < configured delta (e.g., 2%)
circuit_breaker_design: SOFT_OPEN: redirect configurable fraction (default 20%) of traffic away using deterministic hashing + random sample to minimize user impact
OPEN: route returns failover response or is redirected entirely to secondary region/model; record open reason and timestamps
PROBATION: allow small bursts of traffic with success threshold (e.g., 95% success over 2 minutes) to transition back to CLOSED
Reopen backoff: exponential backoff on reopen attempts (base 30s, factor x2, cap 30m) to prevent thrashing
Throttling interactions: when a route is OPEN, apply cluster-level admission control to avoid cascading overloads
observability_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-route and per-region timeline of triggers, mitigation mode, traffic shift %, and model-variant in use
Logs: decision events emitted with route, policy_id, signal_snapshot, chosen_action, and reasoning token
SLO alerts: p95 latency and error-rate burn alerts during mitigation; alerting thresholds default to 50% of SLO budget burn in 5m
Audit: record every automatic swap for post-mortem and quality regression analysis
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): unit and integration tests; run fault-injection scenarios to validate thresholds and state transitions
Phase 2 (canary): enable on <5% of traffic for non-enterprise customers and internal dev teams; monitor dashboards for 48h
Phase 3 (gradual): expand to 25% then 100% of new routes, retain ability to disable per-organization via feature flag
Chaos test: schedule controlled region outages in staging (and optionally in a weekend maintenance window) to validate cutovers
Runbook: attach automated rollback and manual override steps in Console when mitigation is active
implementation_notes: Router changes: add rule-evaluation hook before final routing decision; keep evaluation cost <1% CPU overhead
Data plane: lightweight ring counters for short windows; use Redis/etcd for cross-box aggregates with TTLs
Model variants: maintain catalog metadata (latency, cost, eval-score) to make swap decisions deterministic
Backward compatibility: default policy is monitor-only until policy flag is flipped per route
Security: mitigation actions must be logged to audit logs (for Private deployments we need KMS-backed audit retention; see security doc)
tradeoffs_and_risks: Risk of oscillation if thresholds are too sensitive; mitigated via SOFT_OPEN and backoff
Quality regressions if lower-quality variants are used; mitigated via eval-score gating and per-customer opt-outs
Increased cost when shifting to dedicated/warmer capacity as a mitigation path; require cost guardrails
Cross-region decisions require fast signal propagation; eventual consistency may cause temporary asymmetric behavior
tests_and_validation: Load test scenarios: synthetic 429 flood, tail-latency regression, backend 5xx burst
A/B experiments comparing baseline routing vs threshold-driven mitigations with user-visible error reduction and cost delta metrics
Automated regression tests for state transitions using a simulated time advance harness
Post-deploy: run weekly canary traffic replay from production tails to validate no unexpected quality regressions
